newsitem.title: USA: Carnival says has held talks with Celebrity.
newsitem.headline: Carnival says has held talks with Celebrity.

text.p: Carnival Corp. disclosed on Thursday that it held merger talks with Celebrity Cruises Lines Inc. before launching a $525 million bid aimed at breaking Celebrity's planned $500 million deal with Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd.

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Miami-based Carnival also said it had privately offered to buy Celebrity for $510 million in cash just six days after it struck the June 17 deal with Royal Caribbean.
"We have held conversations on and off for a few years," said Carnival spokesman Tim Gallagher.
Although the talks never resulted in a deal, "our interest in Celebrity is well known to them," he said.

Late Wednesday, Carnival offered to buy privately held Celebrity for $525 million in cash or a cash and stock transaction. The $500 million pact with Royal Caribbean calls for a cash and stock deal, and also calls for the assumption of $800 million in debt.
Celebrity is owned jointly by New York-based Overseas Shipholding Group Ltd. and privately held Chandris group.
A spokesman for Overseas Shipholding on Thursday confirmed that Celebrity had received the Carnival offer.
"We've told them we would contact them if we had any interest in pursuing it," said spokesman Robert Cowen.
Celebrity struck a deal to be acquired by Royal Caribbean for $500 million on June 17.

Royal Caribbean could not be reached for comment. Company executives met with Wall Street analysts on Thursday for a previously scheduled conference, but declined to discuss the competing offer, said analysts who attended the meeting.
Analysts said Carnival has offered a rich price for Celebrity, but noted that the company would not jeopardise earnings for a deal.
Known for financial conservatism, Carnival would likely abandon the effort if it threatened to dilute earnings, said Wall Street analysts who spoke with company officials on Thursday.
"If it works, and it works out to be non-dilutive, it's terrific. If it looks to be dilutive, presumably Carnival will not pursue it," said Joseph Buckley of Bear Stearns & Co. Inc.
A spokesman for Carnival did not comment specifically on whether the company would walk away from a dilutive transaction, saying only "it has been our policy not to do dilutive deals".

Because Celebrity is privately owned, Carnival has limited access to the company's financial performance. In its letter offering $525 million, Carnival said it may be willing to increase the bid if it received access to Celebrity's financial documents.
Analysts said Carnival would likely have little problem integrating Celebrity into its portfolio. Carnival recently completed the acquisition of Italian cruise company Costa Crociere SpA.
"Carnival has done a lot of acquisitions in its day and integrated many brands. If anyone can maximize Celebrity's potential, Carnival can," said Jill Krutick of Smith Barney.

Analysts also said Carnival would gain a valuable presence in the Bermuda market with an acquisition of Celebrity, which holds a 40 percent market share there. Carnival does not have a presence in Bermuda.
Shares of Carnival slipped 56.25 cents to $42.50 on the New York Stock Exchange. Royal Caribbean lost $2.875 to $34 per share, also on NYSE.
